column1: # OCTOPATH TRAVELER: Square Enix / Acquire, Unreal Engine 4.18 (++UE4+Release-4.18; legacy version 4 paks), SDK 3.5.1, NVN, CRIWARE (ADX2 sound, a USM movie); update 1.0.5.
# Started from the NSP script's provisional profile (dm/games/profile_guess.py) and brought up on the Mac (docs/agents)
# subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie (main imports from it)
# menus and the battle commands take the D-pad
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so there is no virtual address memory: this Unreal Engine 4's nninitStartup sets a heap of pool − used (3.08 GB) and runs on it, with no
# engine address region. The 4 GB block of the games without virtual address memory: 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region
# the rewritten modules (about 120 MB) are larger than the default 64 MB of used memory the game takes off the pool for its heap
# Unreal loads its textures from the CPU straight into CPU-uncached pools after creating them and never flushes (its UI images, the world map, the sprite sheets): without both keys
# they stay black or missing (the language notice's pictures, the title logo, the whole traveler selection), as for FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles
# The engine's global shaders (Engine/GlobalShaderCache-GLSL_SWITCH.bin), the engine's own materials and the game's. Unreal Engine 4 keeps every shader inline in the cooked packages,
# zlib-compressed, inside legacy paks whose blocks are zlib-compressed too (shader_split.py ue_legacy_jobs)
